title: Introduce token cost concordance and trace prioritizer
author: Jordan Kim
release_notes: Adds a token-cost concordance index, trace-prioritizer service, new dashboard panels, and tuned alert rules to reduce SLO noise from low-cost churn.
commit_summaries: telemetry: add concordance indexer and schema
service: implement trace prioritizer daemon and APIs
dashboards: new cost-concordance panels and drilldowns
alerts: tune token-cost noise suppression and add dampening rules
tests: add unit + integration + small load harness
description:
Motivation: production token-cost telemetry shows a large volume of low-cost invocations that create noise in SLO alerts and make root-cause work difficult. This PR introduces a token-cost concordance index (a compact, append-only index keyed by invocation shape + model variant + token-range) and a trace prioritizer service that tags/streams only the most informative traces for expensive or anomalous cost patterns.

What changed (high level): concordance indexer writes a compact signature for each invocation and maintains rolling histograms per route/model; a prioritizer daemon subscribes to the index and sampling signals and elevates traces that are high-cost, anomalous by concordance score, or correspond to regressions compared to a 7-day baseline. We also add dashboard panels that join the concordance index with trace metadata for fast drilldowns, and tuned alert rules that apply dampening for low-cost churn while preserving sensitivity to cost regressions.

Compatibility & migration: indexer uses an additive migration (concordance table with TTL) so rollout is non-blocking. A lightweight migration SQL is included and will be applied in background during canary. The prioritizer runs as an opt-in service behind a feature flag.

Testing & validation: unit tests for indexer logic, integration tests exercising real traces through the prioritizer, and a small load harness that simulates token-cost churn and verifies that the prioritizer reduces noise by ~78% while keeping recall >95% for cost regressions. CI run passed.

Rollout plan: canary in us-west-2 dev tenancy for 48h (feature flag on), validate false-positive/negative rates, then ramp to 20%/50%/100% over 48h subject to metrics gating (alert noise, index ingestion lag). If we see increased latency in ingest pipeline, revert to previous sampling policy.

Why unique: combines low-cardinality concordance indexing with a streaming prioritizer to focus telemetry/trace storage budget on impactful invocations; reduces alert noise without blinding ops to real regressions.

Checklist: [x] Indexer code and schema added, [x] Prioritizer daemon, [x] Dashboards and runbook, [x] Alert tuning and CI coverage, [x] Migration SQL and smoke tests, [x] Rollout plan documented.
review_threads: Maya Clarkson: Nice approach — can you clarify storage cost implications? Author: estimated ~0.6GB/day for our dev region with default TTL, added knobs in config to reduce precision.
Ravi Singh: Prioritizer looks async-safe but we should limit backpressure on ingest. Author: added circuit-breaker and backpressure metrics; see services/prioritizer/main.rs.
Elliot Park: Dashboard queries may be heavy on large time ranges. Author: added pre-aggregated rollups and query timeouts; included sample Grafana panel with 30d retention rollup.
Sofia Morales: Are alert dampening windows configurable per-tenant? Author: yes — alert rules accept per-tenant thresholds; defaults applied for small tenants.
Maya Clarkson: Approving after CI green and minor nits fixed.
notes_on_rollout: Canary in us-west-2 on dev tenancy for 48h, then gradual 20/50/100% over two days. Feature-flag controlled; migration runs in background. Monitor ingest-lag, prioritizer-latency, alert-noise-rate.
test_plan: Unit: indexer logic and signature stability
Integration: end-to-end trace prioritization against synthetic traffic
Load: small harness to validate noise reduction and recall
E2E: dashboard panels validate join keys and drilldowns
notes: This PR is focused on observability economics: by indexing invocation shapes and prioritizing traces at ingest time we can reclaim storage and operator attention for signal-rich events.
